text:
dave: Heads-up — we hit another sustained capacity spike yesterday. Hosted GPU pool hit >95% and a small percentage of low-priority requests started timing out. We need a policy that backs down non-critical traffic first, with clear headers/control and observability.

maria: Agreed. Goal: preserve paid-customer SLOs, degrade best-effort traffic gracefully. Prefer header-driven routing so client SDKs can opt into cheaper variants.

chris: Proposal sketch: use a prioritized routing chain keyed by headers (x-customer-tier, x-inference-class), then fall through to cheaper model variants. Example rule: 
```
route {
  match: path("/v1/generate") && header("x-customer-tier") != "enterprise"
  priority: 10
  route_mode: "capacity-aware"
  fallback_chain: ["redwood-small-quant", "redwood-embeddings-only"]
  circuit_breaker: {max_concurrent: 250, window_s: 60}
  header_overrides: {"x-inference-mode": "degraded"}
}
```
This keeps enterprise pinned unless circuit-breaker trips.

alex: Two quick concerns: 1) how do we surface which step served the request in tracing/logs? 2) SDKs might not set x-inference-class — need defaults and server-side tagging.

maria: For tracing, add a response header `x-routing-step` with the final route id and emit a metric `route.fallback_step` with tags {route, reason}. For SDKs, default to `best_effort` when header absent and map anonymous requests to lowest priority.

chris: Also propose a short-circuit rule for extremely constrained pools: if queue_length > 1000 then immediately degrade to embeddings-only for requests with header `x-degrade-allow: true`. That avoids long queuing.

infra-bot: alert: pool(hosted-a) queue_length=1124, util=96% — autodetect threshold breached.

dave: Good. On circuit-breaker behavior: prefer a token-bucket style breaker (graceful ramp down) rather than hard-open, so we can serve a steady controlled stream to backup models. Documentation should call this "soft-open" CB.

maria: UX note for console: in rollout view show a simple toggle for "Backdown strategy" (off / soft-open / hard-open) and a live histogram of requests by fallback step. Engineers should be able to override per-route via a modal that edits header overrides.

alex: Telemetry: emit counters for `fallback.invoked` with tags {from_model,to_model,trigger} and histograms for `latency.by_fallback_step`. Also add sampling for request bodies when fallback is used so QA can validate quality regressions.

chris: About header overrides — we must lock down who can set high-priority headers. If clients can set `x-customer-tier: enterprise` we open ourselves to abuse. Enforce auth-scoped header whitelists on the gateway.

dave: Agreed. Enforcement idea: `auth_policy` includes `allowed_route_headers` per API key. Admin console exposes a list.

maria: Action items: 1) chris — write a POC routing config and integrate `x-routing-step` responses. 2) alex — add telemetry metric names and an initial Grafana dashboard layout. 3) dave — design auth header whitelist and add to gateway. I'll own console UX changes.

chris: I'll push a minimal PR with the route schema and a small simulator to test circuit-breaker soft-open behavior. Expect draft by EOD.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: staging route-sim v0.1 deployed to infra-staging.

dave: Thanks — let's reconvene after the POC. If staging sim shows >10% best-effort degradation improvement without enterprise impact, we ship to canary. :thumbsup:
